chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated that Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Hatam quoted Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Abdul Rahman Abu Yaqoob al-Sameen al-Baqavy, on the authority of Ibn Eliyeh, on the authority of Ibn Oan, on the authority of Al-Sha’abi, on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: 'I was with my father when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: This religion will remain strong and invulnerable, conquering those who oppose it, until there are twelve Caliphs. Then he spoke a word that the people could not hear due to the noise, so I asked my father: What was the word that the people could not hear? He said: He said: They are all from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number and origin of the Caliphs who will lead the Muslim community?
ai.summary: This narration from Jabir ibn Samurah, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, establishes the twelve Caliphs as a definitive eschatological sign, emphasizing that their authority from Quraysh ensures the religion's strength and invincibility. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted as referring to the Twelve Imams, linking the political and spiritual continuity of the Ummah directly to the Prophet's progeny. The mention of 'twelve' serves as a crucial theological anchor for the concept of *Ismah* (infallibility) and divine appointment within the Imamate.
